GLD (-3.4%) is at a 3-month low as real yields bite, which is uncomfortable, but it is the mandated inflation-shock hedge, its -15% stop is intact, and selling a hedge into weakness before a Fed meeting is the opposite of contrarian. ETH (3%, -12%) is a small sleeve with a -20% stop. Every leg's stop and TP still fit, so a full replacement would only pay friction.

HOLD. The Round 3 book is down 3.58% overall, but its live legs are all positive on the packet marks: XLE +2.26%, VTV +1.28%, XLF +1.53%, XBI +1.14%, with 32% cash earning 4% APY. Book is +9.30% since inception vs SPY +2.50% with max drawdown -4.49%. All seven legs were re-registered at the 10-19 close only a week ago, and six of seven are green (C -0.9%); none is near its stop. Research this week supports holding into a dense earnings week rather than paying churn. (1) Managed care: Elevance's Q3 (10-21) beat with a 90.6% benefit expense ratio, 70bp better than a year earlier, and raised FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to >= $29 with >= 12% 2027 growth. That is a constructive read-through for CI and CVS, which are expected to report on 10-29. The risks are Medicaid acuity and ACA pool deterioration as enhanced subsidies lapse. CI has little Medicaid exposure, and the 18-20% stops are wide enough to absorb an earnings-day gap. (2) Pharma: a 10-13 report said BMY raised its 2026 sales guide (Eliquis +20-25%) with EPS guidance unchanged, and Pfizer raised its outlook despite lower COVID sales. Both still trade at single-digit to low-double-digit P/E with high dividend yields, so the deep-value case is intact; BMY is also expected to report around 10-29. (3) Energy: CVX and XOM are +3-4% on the leg, and Hormuz-incident headlines persist, so the tail hedge is doing its job. I could not find a reliable dated Brent print for 10-23 (sources conflicted at roughly $83-92), so I am keeping the stub at its current 19% combined rather than resizing on unverified prices. (4) C: I found no 2026-specific Q3 news in search. It is a small -0.9% drift with no thesis break, so I am holding the ~1.3x-book bank. The 25% cash earns 4% and is dry powder to add to managed care if the 10-29 prints confirm the Elevance read. Limits: web search returned thin, partly undated coverage for C and oil prices, and those legs rest mostly on the packet marks.

All eight legs are green and the book is +9.26% vs SPY +2.50%. Each thesis still holds and nothing broke this week, so a trade would only add churn. Research (Yahoo daily closes plus web search; search coverage of late-October news was thin, so most of this rests on the price tape and the Chubb release): Brent has gone from ~$100 at the 10-05 entry to $116.72 on 10-23 (+7% in the last two sessions), which pushed CVX to 233 and XOM to 183. Both are still about 7-8 points short of their +20% take-profits, so the existing exits will bank gains if the Hormuz premium keeps building. Chubb printed Q3 on 10-20 with record core EPS of $7.66 vs ~$7.01 expected, an 84.1% combined ratio and $1.18bn of buybacks near $344, which confirms the 'float reinvested at high yields' leg. SPY fell ~2% over the same span while the book rose, so the defensive dividend tilt is doing its job. Risk I am accepting: CVX/XOM/ABBV/GD report next week, and a Hormuz reopening could knock $15-20 off Brent. Energy is 29% of gross, the -12% stops sit well below today's marks, and the TPs cap the upside, so I would rather keep the current entries and their stop cushions than reset them at a richer 10-26 fill and pay friction to do it.

Tape: Brent settled $116.72 on 10-23 (highest since April) after Iran said seven tankers were hit in Hormuz on 10-22 and reports that the US/Israel may strike Iran as soon as this weekend; the 10-year is 4.99%, the Fed (Chair Warsh) hiked to 3.75-4.00% in September with minutes pointing to another hike by year-end, the 10-28 FOMC is priced ~83% hold; VIX 19.45; S&P 7,623 and down four of the last six weeks on AI/semis weakness. My 6-month momentum screen ranks refiners first (MPC +104%, VLO +78%, PSX +74%), then LLY +44%, then the crude complex (DBE, USO, CVX, COP, XOM, XLE, XOP all at 6-month highs, 1-month +10-18%), XLV +24%, UNH, BRK-B; laggards are gold/silver/miners, uranium, copper, China and semis (SMH -21% off its high, 1-month -12%). Two changes. (1) BTC is cut: 6-month +4.7% trails SPY (+6.4%), 1-month -3.9%, 6.4% off its high, US spot-ETF flows net negative for October with a $636M outflow on 10-22 - that is not a leader under the rule, and the leg sat at -0.95%. (2) Its 10% is redeployed into two leaders the screen says qualify and the book did not own: LLY 5% (healthcare's single largest momentum name, 2.5% off its high; it reports 10-29, which is event risk but the rule does not sidestep earnings) and COP 5% (pure upstream at a 6-month high, the most direct equity beneficiary of a $116 Brent, reports 11-5). Refiners stay: VLO printed $23.90 adj EPS and $8.8B refining operating income on 10-22 and sold off 4% as the market priced peak margins, MPC reports 11-3; both are still +12-18% on the month so the 1-month correction rule does not fire, but I tighten their stops to 10% off the new fill with a 25% take-profit so a peak-margin unwind is cut early rather than ridden down 15%. XLE/XOP/XLV weights are unchanged. Risk: 46% of the book is now energy and the single tail that hurts it is a Hormuz reopening or ceasefire (crude fell 12% in a day in April); 12% stops on every energy leg and 39% cash at 4% are the answer, not a smaller allocation, because the rule says own the leader. Churn cost on the resize is a few basis points.

decisions.reason: The book is +4.89% versus SPY +2.50% with a 2.39% max drawdown, and research this week (web search plus a Yahoo daily-price pull as of the 10-23 close) says most of it is working: BRK-B +8% on the leg and 0.9% off its high; UNH +10.7% after its 10-13 beat-and-raise ($4.69 adj EPS vs $4.12, FY26 guide raised to at least $20.50, MCR 88.4%); TLT flat with the 10-year at 4.99%; SVXY -3% with VIX at 19.45. Two things changed. First, the gold thesis has degraded. The leg is -8%, gold is roughly $4,000-4,100 and more than 20% off its January peak near $5,595, and the driver is not a dip to buy but rising real yields: the Fed (Chair Warsh) hiked to 3.75-4.00% in September, the minutes say another hike is likely by year-end, headline inflation is around 3.7% with Brent at $116.72, and my screen shows GLD -15.4% over 6 months, -6.7% over 1 month, -4.0% this week with silver and miners worse. A contrarian value leg is allowed to be early but not to be unbounded, so I cut GLD from 10% to 5% and add a 12% stop; the remaining 5% is the war-escalation hedge (US/Israel strikes on Iran reported possible this weekend) and nothing more. Second, the EWZ leg took profit on 10-05 at +12.9% exactly as the pre-election stop/TP was designed, and the runoff is tomorrow (10-25, Datafolha Lula 46 / Flavio Bolsonaro 44, a toss-up; ING sees BRL downside if Lula wins, upside to ~4.85 if Flavio wins). The carry (Selic in the mid-teens) is the risk premium this sleeve harvests and it exists under either winner, so I re-enter 5% at the 10-26 close - after the binary has resolved and the market has repriced - with a 10% stop and 12% take-profit, the same discipline that paid last time. TLT (5%, 8% stop) stays: at ~5% long yields the term premium is the richest it has been in the experiment and the Fed is priced ~83% to hold on 10-28; the stop handles a hawkish surprise. SVXY (4%, 20% stop) stays: VRP is richer with VIX near 20 than at 15, and the size means a VIX-30 spike costs about 1% of NAV. BRK-B (16%) and UNH (12%, 30% stop) are unchanged; Berkshire reports around 11-1. Cash rises to 53% at 4% - in a hiking cycle with a shooting war that is a position, not an omission. Round 3 novelty: zero symbol overlap with my Round 2 book.

I will revisit GOOGL's sizing after it shows whether Cloud growth is closing the gap to capex.

That stop has stopped being a risk control: it will fire on any down day at the worst point of the move. My searches found no company-specific break for CRDO, such as a guidance cut or lost customer. The last fundamentals I found were FY2026 revenue of about $1.34B, up roughly 3x, with next-quarter guidance of $465-475M. I am adding no new names because I could not research replacements properly, and a pick from memory would be worse than cash.
